articleTitle: IEE Colloquium on 'Electronic Information Interchange - X400 and EDI' (Digest No.72)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic Information Interchange 400 and EDI

articleTitle: EDI and X.400: towards unification-technical issues and standards initiatives
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic Information Interchange 400 and EDI
abstract: The author describes a study on electronic data interchange (EDI), and discusses the need to unify standards for EDI and the X.400 recommendation. The study identifies four approaches to using X.400 to support EDI, and the relationship between EDI and X.400 is considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic Information Interchange 400 and EDI
abstract: The author discusses how business requirements, and the underlying IT architecture, show that electronic data interchange (EDI) and X.400 have complementary roles in information interchange within and between system enterprises. Office documentation architecture (ODA) is considered, and progress and future developments are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: EDI and X.400-commercial and strategic issues
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic Information Interchange 400 and EDI
abstract: The author reviews the commercial and strategic issues that are emerging emerging from users' practical experience of electronic data interchange (EDI) and X.400 message handling services. The concept of public X.400 services providing a delivery service for EDI is examined, and the author assesses users' requirements for EDI, and considers the extent to which they are met by public X.400 message handling services.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic Information Interchange 400 and EDI
abstract: The author describes the interdepartmental electronic mail project run by the CCTA that has been in operation since July 1986. The services provided, including an X.400 switch, are considered, and the main problems and future areas for concern are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Unified implementation of X.400 and EDI
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic Information Interchange 400 and EDI
abstract: The author describes an electronic data interchange (EDI) software package which is based on CCITT X.400 protocols and is portable across a wide range of computer system types. The package pays particular attention to the need for flexible design to support the wide variety of X.400-based EDI networks planned for the next few years. Requirements for a high-level EDI application program interface (API) which is independent of the underlying protocols in order to assist migration of EDI application programs from one network to another are also considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Electronic Information Interchange 400 and EDI
abstract: The author examines the practical issues of implementing electronic data interchange (EDI). In order to understand the implications of adopting standards like X.400 for EDI traffic it is necessary to understand the basic issues involved. The author raises some fundamental questions and provides answers which will give a better understanding of these basic issues.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
